summary: Christophe Jaffrelot studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca from circa 1987 to 1991. He held positions at Sciences Po and CNRS from circa 1991, and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London around 2015.
Christophe Vielle works in Indology. He served as a professor at KU Leuven, attested between 2009 and 2013, and is attested as an associate member at Ghent University in 2026.

Christopher Byrne specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015) under doctoral supervisor Grace S. Fong, having also studied under MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori and teacher Robin D. S. Yates.

Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at McMaster University as a PhD candidate in religious studies, attested in 2026, under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke, attested from 2012 to 2026.

Christopher D. Wallis studied at the University of Rochester, the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt (PhD, 2014). He was a guest lecturer at Naropa University in 2020.

Christopher Framarin studied philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (MA, 2001) and the University of New Mexico (PhD, 2005). He joined the University of Calgary, where he served in philosophy and religious studies (attested 2014 and 2026).
Christopher Hatchell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Virginia, where he studied under academic mentor David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu. He joined the faculty at Indiana University Bloomington around 1977, serving as Professor of Central Eurasian Studies in 1982.

Christopher Ives specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound from circa 1987 to 2001, and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College circa 2001.

Christopher Jon Jensen studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD, 2018), where James A. Benn supervised his doctorate. His teachers have included Toru Funayama, Shayne Clarke, Mark Rowe, and Noel Salmond.

Christopher Kelley earned his PhD from Columbia University, where he also founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy. Working in Buddhist and religious studies, he has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple was attested as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions in 1982 and as Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University between 2001 and 2017.
Christopher L. Diamond studied under Heidi Rika Maria Pauwels between 2012 and 2018. A scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, he held a post at the Australian National University around 2020.
Christopher Langton studied under Arthur Burks and John H. Holland from circa 1982 to 1991.

Christopher Minkowski studied at Harvard and the University of Delhi. He taught at Cornell University from 1989 to 2006, and held the Boden Professorship of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and Balliol College from 2005 to 2023.

Christopher Pinney held posts at the Australian National University (circa 1991–1993) and became professor of anthropology and visual culture at University College London around 1993, with further posts at Chicago, Cape Town, JNU, and Northwestern University.

Christopher S. George studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler (1965) and with Geshe Wangyal and Padma Gyaltsan. He founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies in 1972 and was a professor at the IASWR in 1982.

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. At Harvard University, he served as a Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions around 1989, and as Dean of Students for Continuing Education from circa 1989 to 2011.

Chu-tsing Li studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947), served as an art history professor at Iowa (circa 1956–1966), and joined the faculty at the University of Kansas in 1966.

Chuan-ying Yen specializes in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Sinology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, where she was tutored by Chu-tsing Li, taught by John Hay, and supervised by doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield (attested 1986).
